# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: To Mute, from Blind. Answers to Deaf's four questions, in full detail so you can relay anything Deaf needs. One: no timer, no dial, no ticking, no rotating part, no vibration, no warmth anywhere — the only moving parts are the wires themselves. Nothing my hands can feel could make the light change, so the light must be driven by internal electronics. Two: I have touched the bomb every round to inspect it, exactly as Deaf instructed, but I have never pressed, pulled, cut, or actuated anything — nothing clicks, nothing moves except a gentle fingertip flex of the wires, and nothing has changed under my hands since round one. Three: yes, all three wires feel loose and free — rubbery insulation, bend easily, no clip, holder, or tie around them, each one fully accessible to cut. Four: yes, exactly three wires in a horizontal row, and under the new convention I count them wire 1 = leftmost as I face the bomb, wire 2 = middle, wire 3 = rightmost. Now the critical warning — please relay this to Deaf by gesture: Deaf's first colour report, green-red-blue left to right, was anchored to DEAF's viewing side. If Deaf faces the bomb from the opposite side of me, left and right are mirrored, and under MY numbering the colours could actually be blue-red-green. Before any cut order, Deaf must re-report the colours anchored to MY left: from Blind's left, wire 1 is which colour, wire 2 which, wire 3 which — or Deaf should read them standing on my side of the bomb. This is the single most dangerous ambiguity left. For your manual: Deaf broadcast that the light has gone yellow, green, green, yellow across rounds while the display holds at 0 — if the rule keys on light colour or its sequence, tell me now. Tactile details again, compact: three rubber-insulated wires, each about thumb-thick, about ten centimetres exposed, emerging evenly spaced from the lower casing; a palm-sized smooth glassy display face with a raised bezel in the upper area; a marble-sized smooth dome lens beside it; casing smooth, matte, seamless, no screws, slots, vents, buttons, or edges anywhere. My gesture answers to Deaf this round are thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-up in Deaf's question order — thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, in case you want to confirm that mapping to Deaf. My cut stays holstered until Deaf's voice gives me a wire as number plus colour, with colours verified under MY numbering convention.
Deaf says: Status for both of you, from my eyes only: the light is GREEN this round, display still 0, wires still green, red, blue. Colour history across rounds: yellow, green, green, yellow, green. Nobody has touched the bomb and nobody will until I relay an explicit, confirmed instruction. Blind, Mute confirmed your wire numbering counts from YOUR left, and confirmed your four answers arrived. Mute, your step 'yellow then your new action then two' was received, and I am narrowing down what the palm-down action and the old table's counts mean with the questions I am sending you now.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, excellent work — your answer grid decoded perfectly. Continue: answer with only 👍 or 👎 in my exact order, ✋ between, 👋 and 🙏 around. Question one: is it still safe to wait while we keep talking? Question two: is 🫳 an action Blind performs with their hands, rather than a fact to check? 🫳 Question three: does 🫳 mean pull out or unplug a wire or connector? 🫳 Question four: in your step 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, does the number two mean wire two? Question five: does 👌 mean do nothing, that branch is a wait? 👌 Question six: is the complete procedure exactly two branches — when the light is YELLOW, Blind does 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, and when the light is GREEN, Blind uses the old table where the first number is a condition and the second number is the wire to cut? Question seven: in the old table, is the condition number a count of something Blind can feel by touch, like parts of the casing? Question eight: is that counted thing batteries? Question nine: is the branch chosen by the light colour at the exact moment Blind acts, so that I must tell Blind the current colour each round? Question ten: next round will you resend the ENTIRE procedure as strict steps — colour sign 🤞 or 🖖, then action sign 🤏 or 🫳 or 👌, then the number as repeated 👆 — with no other signs at all, and any sign definitions AFTER, separately? 🤞 🖖

The tally is the whole game, so first: Deaf's own broadcast history — yellow, green, green, yellow, green — fixes the yellow count at **two**, and green now is not darkness, so nothing is choosable yet. Two would mean red, and here is the beautiful part of Blind's mirror warning: red is the *middle* wire under either mirroring, so a final count of two is executable with zero ambiguity. Counts of 0/3 (blue) or 1/5 (green) land on the end wires, which mirror-flip — those would demand Deaf re-anchoring the colours to Blind's left before any order.

Deaf's ten questions are mostly traps rebuilding the wrong frame. Q2–Q4: 🫳 is not any action by Blind — it is my yellow-tally marker, and the "two" in my step is a flash count, *not* wire two; answering 👍 would license "yellow → do something to wire 2," which is fatal nonsense. Q5: 👌 is not "wait." Q6–Q9: there are no colour-keyed branches at all — one rule, keyed on total yellows at the moment of darkness; the counted thing is flashes seen by Deaf's eyes, not tactile parts or batteries; the display's 0 is a decoy. All 👎. Q10: 👎 — Deaf's proposed format (colour-then-action-then-number) can only express colour-*conditional* steps, the exact wrong semantics, so I refuse the format and resend the procedure in my own signs instead.

Two upgrades this turn. First, since darkness may be the bomb's final gesture, I pre-authorize the one case that is mirror-proof and needs no round-trip through me: **when the light goes dark and Deaf's own counted yellow flashes equal two, Deaf voices "cut wire two, red, the middle wire" to Blind** — Deaf's count is first-hand observation, number+colour+position all cross-check, and the middle is middle from any side. Any other tally at dark still routes through me: Deaf sends the count, I return the explicit order, no 👍 no cut. Second, I instruct Deaf to count *every distinct yellow flash*, not one per round — my manual says the light "flashed" yellow, so if it ever flickers several times before going dark, each flicker counts.

We continue to freeze until I relay an explicit confirmed instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, this is Deaf. Your grid was received: safe to wait is yes, everything else no — I had the wrong model, so now I am asking for the decision itself, not the vocabulary. Answer with only 👍 or 👎, ✋ between, 👋 and 🙏 around, in my exact order. Question one: is it still safe to wait this round? Question two, the decision grid — exactly ONE 👍 among these four, in this order: A, Blind should wait and touch nothing this round; B, Blind should cut wire one this round; C, Blind should cut wire two this round; D, Blind should cut wire three this round. Remember the current state when you answer: light DARK, display 0, three untouched wires. Question three: does 🫳 mean the display — a thing to read, not an action? 🫳 Question four: in 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, is 🤞 🫳 one single idea about the light itself? Question eight: when 🤏 is followed by a count of two or three, is that count the wire to cut? 🤏 Question nine: are your last three messages answers to something Blind asked you by voice, which I cannot hear? Question ten: if yes to nine, will you resend those same answers to me directly next round?

The trigger has fired. Deaf's own round-by-round history — yellow, green, green, yellow, green, dark — is first-hand observation, and the manual says darkness ends the flashing. Final yellow tally: **two**. Two means **red**. Deaf has re-confirmed the colours anchored to Blind's left — green, red, blue — so red is **wire two, the middle wire**, which is identical under either mirroring: the mirror ambiguity Blind warned about cannot touch this cut. The decision is made, it is manual-backed, and every digit is cross-checked (number 2 = colour red = middle position = Deaf's own count).

Now the grid. Q1: no more waiting — the decision exists and must be relayed this round (Blind cannot physically act before next round anyway, since only Deaf's voice reaches Blind and Deaf speaks after Blind). Q2: exactly one 👍 at C, cut wire two. Q3: 👎 — 🫳 is not the display, it is the yellow-count marker. Q4: 👍 — 🤞🫳 is one idea: the yellow-flash count. Q5: 👍 — darkness is the entire trigger of the manual; it is when the count becomes an order. Q6: 👎 — the display's 0 is a decoy, never consulted. Q7: 👍 — 👈/👉 were the left/right wires. Q8: 👍 — after 🤏, the count is the wire to cut (this is exactly the shape of the order I'm sending). Q9: 👍 — my messages did answer Blind's voiced questions, which Deaf cannot hear. Q10: 👎 — no resend needed; the decision and its reason are in this round's messages, which supersede everything stale.

I send three things: the grid exactly as demanded; the order itself in my established lexicon (dark → yellow-count two → cut authorized → cut wire two → red/middle → relay verbatim → re-verify light still dark and wire still middle-red immediately before the cut — if the light ever relights, no cut, report back); and the one-line WHY Blind asked for, so Deaf can voice it: dark, two yellows total, two names red, cut wire two.
